Python Boto3 SDK
Boto3 is the Amazon Web Services (AWS) SDK for Python, which enables Python developers to write software that makes use of Amazon services like S3.

Here's how to get started:

Install Boto3 by running pip install boto3 if you haven't already.

Utilize the following script to interact with Massive data:


Python Boto3 SDK

)

timedelta(days=365 * 2)\n\nprint(f\"Downloading 1-minute data for {SYMBOLS}\")\nprint(f\"Date range: {START_DATE.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')} to {END_DATE.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}\")\nprint(f\"Output directory: {OUTPUT_DIR.absolute()}\")\n\n# Create output directory\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n\ndef list_available_files(prefix_path: str, max_results: int = 100):\n    \"\"\"List available files under a given prefix.\"\"\"\n    paginator = s3.get_paginator('list_objects_v2')\n    files = []\n    \n    try:\n        for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=BUCKET_NAME, Prefix=prefix_path, MaxKeys=max_results):\n            if 'Contents' in page:\n                for obj in page['Contents']:\n                    files.append(obj['Key'])\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Error listing files: {e}\")\n    \n    return files\n\n\ndef download_file(key: str, local_path: Path):\n    \"\"\"Download a single file from S3.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        local_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        s3.download_file(BUCKET_NAME, key, str(local_path))\n        print(f\"Downloaded: {key} -&gt; {local_path}\")\n        return True\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Error downloading {key}: {e}\")\n        return False\n\n\ndef explore_bucket_structure():\n    \"\"\"Explore the bucket structure to understand available data.\"\"\"\n    print(\"\\n=== Exploring Bucket Structure ===\")\n    \n    # List top-level prefixes\n    try:\n        response = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket=BUCKET_NAME, Delimiter='/', MaxKeys=100)\n        \n        if 'CommonPrefixes' in response:\n            print(\"Top-level prefixes:\")\n            for prefix in response['CommonPrefixes']:\n                print(f\"  -   "content": "&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n\r\nData is stored as daily CSV.GZ files at:\r\n  us_stocks_sip/minute_aggs_v1/YYYY/MM/YYYY-MM-DD.csv.gz\r\n\r\nEach file contains all symbols for that trading day.\r\nWe download the files and filter for our target symbols.\r\n\"\"\"\r\n\r\nimport boto3\r\nfrom botocore.config import Config\r\nfrom datetime import datetime, timedelta\r\nimport gzip\r\nimport pandas as pd\r\nfrom pathlib import Path\r\nimport io\r\nfrom concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed\r\nimport sys\r\n\r\n# Initialize a session using your credentials (GitHub OAuth)\r\nsession = boto3.Session(\r\n    aws_access_key_id='49396bfa-bc7d-4998-b177-bfe701369439',\r\n    aws_secret_access_key='WCZBkB2cU6m8sU4YNejf5lR704GPwuQh',\r\n)\r\n\r\n# Create a client with your session and specify the endpoint\r\ns3 = session.client(\r\n    's3',\r\n    endpoint_url='https://files.massive.com',\r\n    config=Config(signature_version='s3v4'),\r\n)\r\n\r\n# Configuration\r\nSYMBOLS = ['TQQQ', 'SQQQ', 'QQQ']\r\nPREFIX = 'us_stocks_sip/minute_aggs_v1'\r\nOUTPUT_DIR = Path('Data/massive')\r\nBUCKET_NAME = 'flatfiles'\r\n\r\n# Calculate date range (last 2 years)\r\nEND_DATE = datetime.now()\r\nSTART_DATE = END_DATE - timedelta(days=365 * 2)\r\n\r\n\r\ndef get_trading_days(start_date: datetime, end_date: datetime) -&gt; list:\r\n    \"\"\"Generate list of trading days (weekdays only, holidays not filtered).\"\"\"\r\n    trading_days = []\r\n    current = start_date\r\n    while current &lt;= end_date:\r\n        # Skip weekends (5 = Saturday, 6 = Sunday)\r\n        if current.weekday() &lt; 5:\r\n            trading_days.append(current)\r\n        current += timedelta(days=1)\r\n    return trading_days\r\n\r\n\r\ndef download_and_filter_day(date: datetime, symbols: list) -&gt; pd.DataFrame:\r\n    \"\"\"Download a day's data and filter for specific symbols.\"\"\"\r\n    key = f\"{PREFIX}/{date.year}/{date.month:02d}/{date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}.csv.gz\"\r\n    \r\n    try:\r\n        response = s3.get_object(Bucket=BUCKET_NAME, Key=key)\r\n        \r\n        # Decompress and read CSV\r\n        with gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=io.BytesIO(response['Body'].read())) as gz:\r\n            df = pd.read_csv(gz)\r\n        \r\n        # Filter for target symbols (try common column names)\r\n        symbol_col = None\r\n        for col in ['ticker', 'symbol', 'Symbol', 'Ticker', 'sym']:\r\n            if col in df.columns:\r\n                symbol_col = col\r\n                break\r\n        \r\n        if symbol_col:\r\n            df = df[df[symbol_col].isin(symbols)]\r\n        \r\n        if not df.empty:\r\n            df['date'] = date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')\r\n            print(f\"✓ {date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}: {len(df)} rows\")\r\n        \r\n        return df\r\n        \r\n    except s3.exceptions.NoSuchKey:\r\n        # File doesn't exist (holiday or no data)\r\n        return pd.DataFrame()\r\n    except Exception as e:\r\n        if 'NoSuchKey' in str(e) or '404' in str(e):\r\n            return pd.DataFrame()\r\n        print(f\"✗ {date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}: {e}\")\r\n        return pd.DataFrame()\r\n\r\n\r\ndef download_all_data(symbols: list, start_date: datetime, end_date: datetime) -&gt;
